findings.cause: Tooling repair tests require original Magicast/Nx/other reviewed archives through npm pack --offline. pnpm install fills a separate store, so a clean CI runner has no required npm cache entries and fails ENOTCACHED before the Linux job.
findings.fix: Prepare exact provenance-listed archives with SHA-512 verification in a temporary directory, then pass explicit artifact paths into the unchanged repair suites. Explicit reviewed archives still allow offline use. No skip or cache fallback on integrity/network failure.

findings.cause: npm_execpath denotes the parent manager. Under pnpm exec nx it points to pnpm: Cargo invoked pnpm pack with npm-only flags and Android rejected the non-npm parent. Governance contained the same latent assumption.
findings.fix: Resolve the actual npm CLI independently, execute it through Node, and isolate the consumer npm cache. pnpm remains the authoring task manager; these intentionally test npm consumers.

findings.cause: The second setup-node action automatically detects the root pnpm packageManager and invokes pnpm 11 after switching to Node 20. pnpm fails on the unavailable node:sqlite builtin before the Nx17-20 consumer tests start.
findings.fix: Disable automatic package-manager caching only on consumer runtime switches; retain the explicit pnpm cache on the Node24 authoring step. A regression checks this separation in both compatibility jobs.

limitations: Windows/Linux native execution and actual Android Gradle tasks require the hosted rerun.
The first local non-network-enabled consumer attempts hit sandbox cache-write/network restrictions; those attempts are not recorded as passing qualification.
No public npm or shared Yalc publication was performed.
